title: Tech Leads the Way, but One Good Day Doesn't Change the Big Picture
body:
Investors' **risk appetite** returned on Wednesday, as technology shares led a broad advance on Wall Street. The Nasdaq climbed 1.05% to 26,702.86, while the S&P 500 added 0.58% to 7,757.17. Not only did chipmakers rise, but SpaceX also jumped about 7.8% after reporting third-quarter revenue of $14.6 billion, a **substantial** beat over the $12.72 billion that analysts had expected. Its AI business, which brought in $7.6 billion, accounted for more than half of that total.

Not every company shared in the gains, however. Netflix slid 4% to 5% after it cut its advertising revenue forecast to $2.7 billion from $3 billion, a reminder that a weak outlook is punished even in a rising market. Still, strength in chip stocks easily **offset** losses like these, and Meta added to the upbeat mood by rising about 5.8% in after-hours trading. Earlier that day in Seoul, foreign investors bought a net 660 billion won of shares, lifting the KOSPI 3.3% to 5,735.66. Even so, having fallen about 19% from its 20-day high, the index is far from safe, and analysts are not ready to **rule out** another drop. With the 10-year Treasury yield hovering (맴돌다) near 5.15%, a single good day rarely changes the bigger picture. Because investors already expect strong results, much of the good news may be **priced in**; if a big tech company fails to **outperform** those hopes, its stock could easily **take a hit**.
ko:
수요일 투자자들의 위험 선호가 되살아났고, 기술주가 월가의 폭넓은 상승을 이끌었다. 나스닥은 1.05% 오른 26,702.86, S&P500은 0.58% 오른 7,757.17로 마감했다. 반도체주가 올랐을 뿐 아니라, 스페이스X도 3분기 매출 146억 달러를 발표한 뒤 약 7.8% 뛰었는데, 이는 애널리스트 예상치 127.2억 달러를 크게 웃돈 수치다. 76억 달러를 벌어들인 AI 사업이 전체의 절반 이상을 차지했다.

그러나 모든 기업이 상승에 동참한 것은 아니다. 넷플릭스는 광고 매출 전망을 30억 달러에서 27억 달러로 낮춘 뒤 4~5% 하락했는데, 오르는 장에서도 약한 전망은 벌을 받는다는 점을 다시 보여 준다. 그래도 반도체주의 강세가 이런 손실을 넉넉히 상쇄했고, 메타는 시간외 거래에서 약 5.8% 오르며 분위기를 더 띄웠다. 그보다 앞서 서울에서는 외국인이 주식을 6,602억 원 순매수하며 코스피를 3.3% 끌어올려 5,735.66으로 마감시켰다. 그렇지만 20일 고점 대비 약 19% 떨어져 있는 지수는 안심할 단계가 아니며, 애널리스트들은 추가 하락 가능성을 배제하지 않는다. 미 10년물 금리가 5.15% 근처에서 맴도는 한, 하루의 좋은 장이 큰 그림을 바꾸는 일은 드물다. 투자자들이 이미 좋은 실적을 기대하고 있기 때문에 호재의 상당 부분은 주가에 반영돼 있을 수 있고, 빅테크 기업이 그 기대를 넘어서지 못하면 주가가 쉽게 타격을 입을 수 있다.

vocab.en_easy: How willing investors are to buy risky things like stocks instead of safe things like bonds.
vocab.ex: When risk appetite is low, people move their money into cash and bonds.

vocab.en_easy: To do better than expected or better than others.
vocab.ex: Chip stocks outperformed the rest of the market this week.

vocab.en_easy: Already included in the current price because everyone expected it.
vocab.ex: The rate cut was already priced in, so the stock barely moved.

vocab.en_easy: Large in size, amount, or importance.
vocab.ex: I've made substantial progress on my deadlift since I started tracking every set.

vocab.en_easy: To balance one thing with another so the bad effect becomes smaller.
vocab.ex: Gains in my US stocks offset the losses in my Korean ones.

vocab.en_easy: To decide that something is not possible.
vocab.ex: I can't rule out going to Busan this weekend if the weather's nice.

vocab.en_easy: To be hurt or damaged, often by losing money or value.
vocab.ex: My running routine took a hit when it rained all week.

grammar.quote: …foreign investors bought a net 660 billion won of shares, lifting the KOSPI 3.3% to 5,735.66. / Even so, having fallen about 19% from its 20-day high, the index is far from safe…
grammar.explain_ko: 접속사+주어를 지우고 동사를 -ing로 바꿔 문장을 압축한다. ', lifting ~'은 앞 동작의 결과(그래서 ~하게 했다), 'having fallen'은 주절보다 '먼저' 일어난 일(이미 떨어진 상태라서)을 나타낸다. 주어가 주절과 같아야 한다 — 'having fallen'의 주어 = the index.
examples: Prices rose sharply, pushing many investors to sell.
Having run for almost an hour, I was totally soaked, but I felt amazing. (OPIc 과거 경험)

grammar.quote: Not only did chipmakers rise, but SpaceX also jumped about 7.8%…
grammar.explain_ko: 부정어(Not only, Never, Only when 등)가 문장 맨 앞에 오면 의문문처럼 '조동사+주어' 순서로 뒤집힌다. 일반동사 과거면 did를 꺼내고 동사는 원형(did chipmakers rise). 수능 어법 단골: 'Not only chipmakers rose'(X).
examples: Not only did the company miss its target, but it also cut its forecast.
Not only is my gym close to my place, but it's also open 24 hours. (OPIc 묘사)

tense.why_ko: '예상한 것'은 실적 발표(과거)보다 더 먼저 일어난 일이라서 had expected. 기준 시점(발표)보다 한 칸 더 과거.

tense.sentence: …a weak outlook is punished even in a rising market.
tense.why_ko: 특정한 날의 사건이 아니라 '늘 그렇다'는 일반적 사실이라 현재형, 전망이 '벌을 받는' 대상이라 수동태.

review.q: I'm not selling and I'm not buying more, either. I'm just going to ______ until the earnings come out.
review.exp_ko: sit tight = 아무것도 안 하고 버티며 기다리다. '팔지도 사지도 않는다'+'until'(그때까지 기다림)이 단서. jump ship은 '팔고 떠나다'라 앞 문장과 모순, play it safe는 '안전한 쪽을 택하다'(방어주로 갈아타기 등 행동 포함 가능)라 '무행동'이 아님, get crushed는 '박살나다'로 의지 표현에 안 맞음.

review.q: 'The airline added a fuel surcharge to every ticket.' 에서 surcharge와 뜻이 가장 가까운 것은?
choices: a basic fare that replaces the ticket price
a refundable deposit paid in advance
a tax the government collects on fuel
an extra fee added on top of the regular price
review.exp_ko: sur-(위에, 더)+charge(요금) = 기본 요금 위에 얹는 추가 요금. ①은 '대체하는 기본 요금'(base charge 쪽), ②는 돌려받는 보증금, ③은 정부가 걷는 세금 — 항공사가 직접 붙이는 할증료와는 다르다.

review.q: When the stock dipped below $50, retail investors ______ it, pushing the price right back up.
review.exp_ko: pile into = (우르르) 몰려들어 사다. 뒤의 'pushing the price right back up'(가격을 다시 밀어올림)이 단서 — 매수가 몰려야 오른다. 나머지 셋(빠져나오다·포기하다·물러나다)은 모두 매도·이탈이라 가격 상승과 모순.

quiz.q:
[어휘] 문맥상 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
"Even so, having fallen about 19% from its 20-day high, the index is far from safe, and analysts are not ready to ______ another drop."
quiz.exp_ko: '아직 안전하지 않다' → 추가 하락 가능성을 '배제할' 준비가 안 됐다 = rule out. point out(지적하다)은 아직 일어나지 않은 하락을 '지적'할 수 없어 어색, carry out(실행하다)은 하락의 주체가 애널리스트가 아님, figure out(알아내다)은 '준비가 안 됐다'와 논리가 안 맞는다.

quiz.q:
[어법] 다음 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?
"Not only (A)did chipmakers rise, but SpaceX also jumped after (B)reporting revenue of $14.6 billion, a figure (C)that analysts had not expected. Its AI business, which brought in $7.6 billion, (D)accounting for more than half of that total."
quiz.exp_ko: 두 번째 문장의 주어 Its AI business 뒤에 ', which ~,'는 삽입절일 뿐이라 본동사가 필요 → accounted. (A) 부정어 Not only 도치로 did+주어+원형 맞음, (B) 전치사 after 뒤 동명사 맞음, (C) expected의 목적어가 빠진 목적격 관계대명사 that 맞음.

quiz.q: [요지] 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 하루의 강한 반등만으로는 시장의 큰 흐름이 바뀌었다고 보기 어렵다.
기술주 강세가 이어지는 한 코스피도 곧 이전 고점을 되찾을 것이다.
상승장에서는 실적 전망을 낮춘 기업도 투자자에게 덜 외면받는다.
외국인 순매수가 늘면 금리 부담과 관계없이 지수는 계속 오른다.
quiz.exp_ko: 글은 '좋은 하루' 사실을 늘어놓은 뒤 However·Even so로 돌아서 '19% 하락 상태·5.15% 금리·이미 반영된 기대' → 하루 반등이 큰 그림을 바꾸진 않는다로 결론. ②는 '배제 못 한다'는 추가 하락과 반대, ③은 넷플릭스 사례('상승장에서도 벌받는다')와 정반대, ④는 금리를 위험 요인으로 든 본문과 모순.

quiz.q: [내용 추론] 본문의 숫자로 판단할 때 옳은 것은?
choices: SpaceX's AI business made up less than half of its quarterly revenue.
SpaceX's revenue beat analysts' estimate by more than $2 billion.
Netflix's new ad revenue forecast is 10% lower than its previous one.
The Nasdaq's percentage gain was more than twice that of the S&P 500.

talk.topic: Beats and misses — SpaceX는 날고 넷플릭스는 미끄러진 날
talk.setting_ko: 목요일 아침 출근길, 주식 하는 회사 동기 두 명(A·B)이 지하철에서 밤사이 미국장 얘기를 한다.

dialogue.en: Did you see SpaceX last night? It's been on a tear since the earnings came out.
dialogue.ko: 어젯밤 스페이스X 봤어? 실적 나오고 나서 완전 질주 중이야.

dialogue.en: Yeah, revenue blew past expectations. Like, almost two billion dollars more than people thought.
dialogue.ko: 응, 매출이 예상을 훌쩍 넘었더라. 사람들 생각보다 거의 20억 달러나 더.

dialogue.en: Netflix was the opposite, though. They lowered their ad forecast and the stock slid.
dialogue.ko: 넷플릭스는 반대였어. 광고 전망을 낮췄더니 주가가 미끄러졌어.

dialogue.en: So it was kind of a mixed bag. Good for chips, not so great for streaming.
dialogue.ko: 그러니까 좀 엇갈린 날이네. 반도체엔 좋고 스트리밍엔 별로고.

dialogue.en: And the KOSPI bounced over three percent yesterday. Should I buy more?
dialogue.ko: 코스피도 어제 3% 넘게 튀었잖아. 더 살까?

dialogue.en: I wouldn't read too much into one day. It's still way below where it was a few weeks ago.
dialogue.ko: 하루 가지고 너무 의미 두진 않을래. 몇 주 전보다 아직 한참 아래잖아.

dialogue.en: Fair enough. Maybe I'll hold off on buying until the big tech earnings are done.
dialogue.ko: 맞는 말이다. 빅테크 실적 끝날 때까지 매수는 좀 미뤄야겠다.

dialogue.en: Same here. No need to rush.

expressions.ex: My favorite team has been on a tear lately — five wins in a row.
The concert blew past my expectations. I'd totally go again.

expressions.ko: 좋은 것과 나쁜 것이 섞인 것, 엇갈린 결과
expressions.when_ko: 한마디로 좋다/나쁘다 말하기 어려울 때 (OPIc 평가 답변에 유용)
expressions.ex: The trip was a mixed bag — great food, but terrible weather.

expressions.en: I wouldn't read too much into ~
expressions.when_ko: 한 번의 결과로 결론 내리지 말자고 할 때
expressions.ex: I wouldn't read too much into one bad workout. Everyone has off days.
I'm holding off on buying new running shoes until the sale starts.

your_turn.q_en: When you hear good or bad news about a company you invest in, how do you usually react? Do you act right away or wait?
your_turn.hint_ko: 내 반응 습관(바로 vs 기다림) → 이유 → 짧은 실제 예시 1개 → 앞으로 어떻게 할지. 오늘 표현 2개 이상(a mixed bag, hold off on, I wouldn't read too much into) 넣기.
your_turn.sample_answer: Honestly, I used to react way too fast. If a stock dropped, I'd sell it the same day. But these days I try not to read too much into one piece of news. Last week, for example, the market was a mixed bag, and I almost sold everything, but I held off on it for a few days, and things calmed down. So now my rule is simple: wait at least a day, check the numbers, and then decide.

talk.topic: 공원 저녁 러닝 — 처음 만난 러닝 크루와 페이스 맞추기
talk.setting_ko: 평일 저녁, 동네 강변 공원. 혼자 조깅하던 A가 러닝 크루 멤버 B를 따라 처음으로 같이 뛴다.

dialogue.en: Hey, you're new, right? We're doing an easy 5K tonight. Wanna join?
dialogue.ko: 안녕하세요, 처음 오셨죠? 오늘은 가볍게 5킬로 뛰어요. 같이 하실래요?

dialogue.en: Sure, but I'm not sure I can keep up with you guys.
dialogue.ko: 좋아요, 근데 제가 여러분 따라갈 수 있을지 모르겠어요.

dialogue.en: Don't worry, it's a chatty pace. Just pace yourself for the first two kilometers.
dialogue.ko: 걱정 마세요, 수다 떨 수 있는 속도예요. 처음 2킬로만 페이스 조절하세요.

dialogue.en: (after a while) Wow, okay… I'm totally winded. That hill was no joke.
dialogue.ko: (잠시 후) 와… 완전 숨차요. 그 언덕 장난 아니네요.

dialogue.en: Ha, everyone says that. Let's walk for a minute. You're doing great, by the way.
dialogue.ko: 하하, 다들 그래요. 1분만 걸어요. 그리고 잘하고 계세요.

dialogue.en: Thanks. My calves are burning, though.
That's normal. Okay, that's 5K — let's call it a day and stretch.
dialogue.ko: 정상이에요. 자, 5킬로 끝 — 오늘은 여기까지 하고 스트레칭해요.

dialogue.en: That was fun. Same time next week?

expressions.ex: It's hard to keep up with all the new apps these days.

expressions.when_ko: 운동·일을 처음부터 너무 세게 하지 말라고 할 때
expressions.ex: It's a long hike, so pace yourself.

expressions.when_ko: 뛰거나 계단을 올라 숨이 찰 때 (out of breath보다 구어적)
expressions.ex: I took the stairs to the tenth floor and I was totally winded.
We've been studying for three hours. Let's call it a day.
That was a great session. Same time next week?

your_turn.q_en: Tell me about the last time you went jogging or walking in a park. Where did you go, and how did it go?
your_turn.hint_ko: 과거 시제로: 언제·어디 → 코스·날씨 → 힘들었던 순간(winded, calves burning) → 끝나고 기분. 4~6문장.
your_turn.sample_answer: So the last time I went jogging was, like, last Sunday evening. I went to the park by the river near my place, which has this long running track. It was a bit chilly, so I decided to pace myself at first. But there's this one hill in the middle, and by the top I was totally winded, you know. My calves were burning. After about five kilometers, I just called it a day and stretched on a bench. I felt so refreshed afterward, though.

opic.survey_topic: 돌발 주제 — 기술(스마트폰·앱·AI) · 목요일 돌발 세트 (헬스 서베이 #51 연결)

combo.q_en: Now let's talk about technology. What kinds of technology do people in your country use these days? Tell me about one piece of technology that you use every day and how you use it.
combo.q_ko: 이제 기술에 대해 얘기해 봅시다. 요즘 당신 나라 사람들은 어떤 기술을 쓰나요? 매일 쓰는 기술 하나와 그것을 어떻게 쓰는지 말해 주세요.
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(한국 사람들 전반: 스마트폰·앱 한 줄) → 본문 ① 내가 매일 쓰는 것 = 운동 기록 앱(+스마트워치) ② 구체적 사용 장면(세트·무게·러닝 페이스 기록, progressive overload 확인) ③ 왜 좋은지·감정 → 마무리(없으면 어떨지 한 줄). 현재시제 일관, 90초~2분. IH/AL 포인트: '일반론 → 나'로 좁히기, 숫자·근육 이름으로 구체화, 필러·자기수정 1회.
combo.model_answer: Well, in Korea, pretty much everyone uses a smartphone for everything — paying, ordering food, taking the subway, you name it. But if I had to pick one piece of technology I use every single day, it'd be my workout app. Actually, it's more like the app plus my smartwatch, because they work together. So when I'm at the gym, I log every set: the exercise, the weight, and how many reps I did. For example, on leg day I'll write down my squats for my quads and glutes, and then Romanian deadlifts for my hamstrings. The thing is, I follow progressive overload, which basically means adding a little more weight or one more rep each week. Without the app, I'd totally forget what I lifted last time. And when I go jogging in the park, the watch tracks my pace and my heart rate, so I can see if I'm getting faster. I mean, it sounds kind of nerdy, but seeing those numbers go up keeps me motivated. Honestly, I can't imagine working out without it now.

key_phrases.en: If I had to pick one, it'd be ~
I can't imagine ~ing without it now.
key_phrases.ko: 이제 그거 없이 ~하는 건 상상도 못 해요

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 '앱을 써요, 좋아요'에서 끝. IH는 사용 장면을 순서대로(헬스장 → 공원), AL은 거기에 progressive overload처럼 '왜 그 기능이 나한테 중요한지'를 한 문장 원리 설명으로 붙인다.

combo.q_en: Have you ever had a problem with a piece of technology? Tell me about a time when something went wrong. What happened, and how did you deal with it?
combo.q_ko: 기술 기기 때문에 문제를 겪은 적이 있나요? 뭔가 잘못됐던 때를 말해 주세요. 무슨 일이 있었고, 어떻게 해결했나요?
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(언제·무엇이 고장 났는지 한 줄) → 본문 ① 배경(무슨 상황이었나: 과거진행 was ~ing) ② 문제 발생 순간(감정: panicked, frustrated) ③ 해결 과정(시도 1 실패 → 시도 2 성공, 과거완료 1회) → 마무리(교훈·지금 습관 = 현재시제). IH/AL 핵심: 과거 시제 흔들리지 않기, 사건 순서 연결어(At first / Then / In the end), 감정 단어 2개.
combo.model_answer: Oh, yeah, this happened just a few months ago. I was getting ready for a half-marathon in my city, and I'd been using my smartwatch to track all my training runs for, like, two months. So on race day, I was at the starting line, and my watch just… died. The screen went black. I had charged it the night before — or at least I thought I had. Anyway, I totally panicked, because I had no idea what my pace was. At first, I tried restarting it a few times, but nothing worked. Then I thought, okay, forget it, and I just borrowed my friend's phone app at the halfway point to check my time. In the end, I actually finished about two minutes faster than my goal, which was kind of funny. Long story short, I learned that I depend on technology way too much. Now I always double-check the battery the night before, and honestly, I sometimes run without the watch just to listen to my body.

key_phrases.en: — or at least I thought I had.

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 '고장 났다 → 고쳤다' 두 문장. IH는 배경-사건-해결 3단, AL은 과거완료(had charged, had been using)로 시간 층을 쌓고 '그 뒤로 바뀐 내 습관'을 현재시제로 닫는다.

combo.q_en: These days, a lot of people are talking about artificial intelligence. What are some concerns people have about AI? How do you personally feel about it?
combo.q_ko: 요즘 많은 사람들이 인공지능에 대해 이야기합니다. 사람들이 AI에 대해 어떤 우려를 갖고 있나요? 당신은 개인적으로 어떻게 생각하나요?
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(이슈 인정 + 시간 벌기 한 줄) → 본문 ① 사회적 우려 2가지(일자리, 가짜 정보) — 'Some people worry that ~' ② 반대 측면(편리함, 예: 운동 앱·투자 정보 요약) ③ 내 입장(균형: 도구로 쓰되 의존은 경계) → 마무리(미래 전망: will/I think ~ is going to). IH/AL 핵심: 개인 이야기만 하지 말고 '사회 → 나' 두 층, 양보 표현(Even though, On the bright side), 미래 시제 1회.
combo.model_answer: Hmm, that's a tough one, but let me think. I'd say the biggest concern is jobs. A lot of people worry that AI is going to replace office workers, like people who do customer service or simple data work. And another thing is fake information. You know, these days AI can make videos and news that look totally real, so it's getting harder to tell what's true. On the bright side, though, AI makes everyday life way easier. For example, I use it to summarize market news before work, and it even suggests changes to my workout plan when I hit a plateau. So personally, I feel kind of mixed about it. I mean, it's a great tool, but I don't want to depend on it for everything, especially big decisions like investing my money. I think in the next few years, AI is going to be everywhere, so the important thing is to learn how to use it wisely instead of just being scared of it.

key_phrases.en: That's a tough one, but let me think.
key_phrases.ko: 어려운 질문이네요, 잠깐 생각해 볼게요 (돌발 질문 시간 벌기)

key_phrases.en: A lot of people worry that ~
I feel kind of mixed about it.

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 '좋기도 하고 나쁘기도 해요'. IH는 우려 2개+장점 1개를 예시와 함께, AL은 마지막에 '미래 전망 + 내 대처법'까지 미래 시제로 말해 의견을 완결한다.
